newsitem.title: USA: PanAmSat sees delay in satellite delivery.
newsitem.headline: PanAmSat sees delay in satellite delivery.

text.p: PanAmSat Corp said on Friday that it expects a delay in completion and delivery of its PAS-7 Indian Ocean Region Satellite.

Delivery of the communications satellite is expected in December 1997 and the launch is anticipated in the first quarter of 1998, PanAmSat said. The launch was previously scheduled for launch in late 1997, PanAmSat said.

Kevin Burgoyne, a company spokesman, said the delay would result in the deferral of the revenues during the time the satellite is grounded, but total revenues generated from the satellite would be unaffected.
PanAmSat also said Space Systems/Loral, a unit of Loral Space and Communications Ltd that is building the PAS-7, said the satellite is expected to exceed its weight specifications.
PanAmSat is exploring several options so the weight of the satellite does not affect its lifespan, since a heavier satellite requires increased launcher power and more fuel, Burgoyne said.
PanAmSat is considering modifications by Space Systems/Loral or the use of an alternative Ariane 4 launcher for the satellite, PanAmSat said.
PanAmSat revised its launch schedule for future satellites as follows: PAS-5 for the Atlantic Ocean region, July 1997; PAS-6 for the Atlantic Ocean region, May 1997; PAS-8 for second quarter 1998.
PanAmSat presently operates a four satellite global system, it said.
